rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice for behaviour or expressions aimed at winning someone’s favour.

example.english: He keeps buying coffee for the boss, trying to be ingratiating.
example.traditional: 佢成日買咖啡畀老闆，想討好佢。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 maai5 gaa3 fe1 bei2 lou5 baan2 soeng2 tou2 hou2 keoi5

rows.note: Choose this when the ingratiating behaviour specifically involves flattering someone, often insincerely.

example.english: He keeps telling the boss he looks handsome; he is obviously being ingratiating.
example.traditional: 佢成日讚老闆靚仔，明顯係奉承。
example.jyutping: keoi5 seng4 jat6 zaan3 lou5 baan2 leng3 zai2 ming4 hin2 hai6 fung6 sing4

rows.note: Use this for strongly disapproving, sycophantic ingratiation, especially toward someone powerful.

example.english: Whenever he sees the department head, he starts being ingratiating and says everything is great.
example.traditional: 佢一見到部門主管就即刻擦鞋，乜都話好。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou2 bou6 mun4 zyu2 gun2 zau6 zik1 hak1 caat3 haai4 mat1 dou1 waa6 hou2
